questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built over many centuries.
- Its total length, including all branches, is about 21,000 kilometers.
- Much of the best-preserved section was built during the Ming dynasty (1368–1644).
questions.stem_md: The student wants to emphasize the wall’s length. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries.
Including all its branches, the Great Wall of China stretches about 21,000 kilometers.
Much of the Great Wall’s best-preserved section dates from the Ming dynasty.
The Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644.
questions.explanation_md: The goal is to emphasize length, and only choice B gives the wall’s length (about 21,000 km).

distractor_notes.A: This is about construction time, not length.
distractor_notes.C: This is about the best-preserved section, not length.
distractor_notes.D: This gives the dynasty’s dates, not the wall’s length.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Sea otters use rocks as tools.
- An otter floats on its back, places a rock on its chest, and strikes shellfish against it to crack them open.
- Some otters keep a favorite rock in a pouch of skin under their forearm.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to explain how sea otters use rocks to open shellfish. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Sea otters are among the animals known to use tools.
Some sea otters keep a favorite rock in a pouch under their forearm.
Floating on its back, a sea otter places a rock on its chest and strikes shellfish against it until they crack open.
Sea otters often float on their backs.
questions.explanation_md: The goal is to explain *how* otters open shellfish. Choice C describes the process step by step.

distractor_notes.A: This says otters use tools but not how.
distractor_notes.B: This describes where an otter keeps a rock, not how it uses it.
distractor_notes.D: This leaves out the rock and the shellfish.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun.
- Neptune is the planet farthest from the Sun.
- Mercury completes an orbit in 88 Earth days.
- Neptune completes an orbit in about 165 Earth years.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to contrast the orbital periods of the two planets. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, and Neptune is the farthest.
Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun.
Both Mercury and Neptune orbit the Sun.
While Mercury orbits the Sun in just 88 Earth days, Neptune takes about 165 Earth years.
questions.explanation_md: To contrast orbital periods, you need both periods set against each other. Choice D gives both and uses “While” to mark the contrast.

distractor_notes.A: This contrasts distance from the Sun, not orbital period.
distractor_notes.B: This gives only one planet’s period.
distractor_notes.C: This notes a similarity instead of a contrast.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- *Frankenstein* is a novel by Mary Shelley.
- It was first published in 1818.
- Shelley began writing it when she was 18 years old.
- It is often called one of the first science fiction novels.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to introduce the novel to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Shelley began writing it when she was 18.
Mary Shelley’s *Frankenstein*, first published in 1818, is often called one of the first science fiction novels.
It was first published in 1818.
Science fiction is a popular genre today.
questions.explanation_md: An introduction for newcomers should name the work and its author and say what it is. Choice B gives the title, author, date, and its significance.

distractor_notes.A: “It” assumes the reader already knows which novel is meant, and the novel isn’t named.
distractor_notes.C: This doesn’t name the novel or its author.
distractor_notes.D: This doesn’t mention the novel at all.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- The axolotl is a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City.
- Unlike most salamanders, it keeps its gills and lives in water its whole life.
- Axolotls can regrow lost limbs, parts of their hearts, and even parts of their brains.
- Scientists study axolotls to learn about tissue regeneration.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to explain why scientists are interested in axolotls. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The axolotl is a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City.
Unlike most salamanders, the axolotl keeps its gills its whole life.
Because axolotls can regrow limbs and even parts of their hearts and brains, scientists study them to learn about tissue regeneration.
Axolotls live in water their whole lives.
questions.explanation_md: The goal is the *reason* for scientists’ interest. Choice C links the axolotl’s regrowth abilities to research on regeneration.

distractor_notes.A: This gives the axolotl’s habitat, not scientists’ interest.
distractor_notes.B: This is an interesting trait, but the notes don’t connect it to research.
distractor_notes.D: This is about habitat, not research.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Two bridges cross the Arlo River in the town of Westmere.
- The Stone Bridge was built in 1847 and is 40 meters long.
- The Harbor Bridge was built in 1998 and is 310 meters long.
- The Harbor Bridge carries four lanes of traffic; the Stone Bridge is open only to pedestrians.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how the two bridges are used. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Stone Bridge was built in 1847, while the Harbor Bridge was built in 1998.
The Harbor Bridge, at 310 meters, is much longer than the 40-meter Stone Bridge.
Westmere’s Harbor Bridge carries four lanes of traffic, whereas its older Stone Bridge is open only to pedestrians.
Both bridges cross the Arlo River in Westmere.
questions.explanation_md: “How the bridges are used” means traffic versus pedestrians. Choice C contrasts exactly that.

distractor_notes.A: This contrasts when they were built, not how they’re used.
distractor_notes.D: This is a similarity, not a difference.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Composer Ines Varga wrote a symphony based on recordings of her hometown.
- She recorded church bells, market vendors, and the sound of a nearby river.
- The orchestra imitates these sounds with instruments.
- The symphony premiered in 2019 and was performed in twelve countries by 2023.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to describe the symphony’s source material. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Ines Varga’s symphony premiered in 2019.
By 2023, Varga’s symphony had been performed in twelve countries.
Varga’s symphony is performed by an orchestra.
Varga based her symphony on recordings of her hometown’s church bells, market vendors, and river.
questions.explanation_md: “Source material” is what the symphony was based on. Choice D names the hometown recordings and what they captured.

distractor_notes.A: This gives the premiere date, not the source material.
distractor_notes.B: This describes the symphony’s reception, not its source.
distractor_notes.C: This is too general and doesn’t mention the source material.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Researchers tested a new kind of solar panel in two cities.
- In Phoenix, the panels produced 22% more electricity than standard panels.
- In Seattle, they produced 9% more electricity than standard panels.
- The new panels capture more light on cloudy days, but Phoenix has far more sunny days.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to present the study’s overall finding. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The new solar panels outperformed standard panels in both cities tested, producing 22% more electricity in Phoenix and 9% more in Seattle.
Phoenix has more sunny days than Seattle does.
Researchers tested solar panels in Phoenix.
Standard solar panels capture less light on cloudy days.
questions.explanation_md: The overall finding is that the new panels beat standard panels in both cities. Choice A states that and gives the numbers.

distractor_notes.B: This is background about the cities, not the finding.
distractor_notes.C: This mentions only one city and gives no result.
distractor_notes.D: This is an inference about standard panels, not the study’s finding.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Tardigrades are microscopic animals about 0.5 millimeters long.
- They can survive being dried out for years by entering a state called cryptobiosis.
- In cryptobiosis, their metabolism drops to less than 0.01% of normal.
- Researchers have revived tardigrades that were dried out for over ten years.
- Scientists hope to use similar methods to preserve vaccines without refrigeration.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to explain a practical application of research on tardigrades. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Tardigrades, microscopic animals about 0.5 millimeters long, can survive being dried out for years.
Researchers have revived tardigrades that were dried out for more than a decade.
Because tardigrades survive drying by slowing their metabolism almost to a stop, scientists hope similar methods could let vaccines be stored without refrigeration.
In cryptobiosis, a tardigrade’s metabolism falls to less than 0.01% of normal.
questions.explanation_md: A “practical application” means a real-world use. Only choice C mentions one—storing vaccines without refrigeration—and it connects that use to how tardigrades survive.

distractor_notes.A: This describes the animal and its ability, with no application.
distractor_notes.B: This is a research result, not an application.
distractor_notes.D: This explains the mechanism but not how people might use it.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- The Voynich manuscript is a handwritten book dated to the early 1400s.
- It is written in an unknown script that no one has deciphered.
- It contains drawings of plants that don’t match any known species.
- Some researchers think the text encodes a real language; others think it is meaningless.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to emphasize the uncertainty surrounding the manuscript. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Voynich manuscript is a handwritten book from the early 1400s.
The Voynich manuscript contains many drawings of plants.
Written in an undeciphered script and illustrated with unidentifiable plants, the Voynich manuscript has left researchers divided over whether its text means anything at all.
Some researchers believe that the Voynich manuscript encodes a real language.
questions.explanation_md: Choice C brings together three sources of uncertainty from the notes: the undeciphered script, the unidentifiable plants, and the researchers’ disagreement.

distractor_notes.A: This gives the manuscript’s date, with no uncertainty.
distractor_notes.B: This mentions the drawings but not that the plants can’t be identified.
distractor_notes.D: This gives only one side of the debate, so the uncertainty isn’t clear.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- In 2021, the town of Brookfield replaced its lawn-mowing schedule in parks with “no-mow” zones.
- Within two years, bee species counted in the parks rose from 14 to 31.
- The town also saved about \$40,000 a year on mowing.
- Some residents complained that the parks looked untidy.
- The town added signs explaining the purpose of the zones.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to present Brookfield’s program as a success while acknowledging a concern. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Brookfield’s no-mow zones more than doubled the number of bee species in its parks and saved about \$40,000 a year, though some residents complained that the parks looked untidy.
Some Brookfield residents complained that the town’s parks looked untidy.
In 2021, Brookfield replaced its lawn-mowing schedule with no-mow zones.
The number of bee species in Brookfield’s parks rose from 14 to 31 in two years.
questions.explanation_md: The goal has two parts: show success and acknowledge a concern. Choice A gives the successes (more bee species, savings) and the complaint.

distractor_notes.C: This describes the program without saying whether it succeeded.
distractor_notes.D: This shows success but leaves out the concern.

questions.passage_md:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Printmaker Kenji Mori and painter Elena Ruiz both depicted the same mountain.
- Mori made 36 woodblock prints of it, each from a different viewpoint.
- Ruiz painted it 36 times from the same window, in different seasons and light.
- Both series were exhibited together in 2022.
questions.stem_md: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the two artists’ approaches. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Both Mori and Ruiz made 36 images of the same mountain.
Mori’s prints and Ruiz’s paintings were exhibited together in 2022.
Mori made 36 woodblock prints of the mountain, each from a different viewpoint.
Whereas Mori varied his viewpoint, showing the mountain from 36 different places, Ruiz kept hers fixed, painting it from one window as the seasons and light changed.
questions.explanation_md: Choice D contrasts their *approaches*: Mori changed where he stood, while Ruiz stayed in one place and let time and light change. That is the key difference in method.

distractor_notes.B: This is a fact about the exhibition, not their approaches.
distractor_notes.C: This describes only Mori’s approach, so there’s no contrast with Ruiz.
